title: Lab 228 - Linux Disk Partitioning - Using gdisk

lab_objective.description: By completing this lab, you will learn how to:
scenario: You are working as a Linux system administrator for a company that needs to prepare a new disk for application data. A new 2 GB disk has been attached to the server as /dev/sdb. Your task is to use gdisk to create a GPT partition table and configure multiple partitions according to the application's requirements. The partitions must be created without modifying the existing operating-system disk.

tasks.title: Identify the available disks on the system
steps: Use an appropriate command to display disk names.
Hint: lsblk
Identify the newly attached 2 GB disk that will be used for this lab.
Do not modify /dev/sda or any disk containing the operating system.
Work only with the newly attached disk /dev/sdb.

tasks.title: Verify that /dev/sdb is the disk intended for this lab
steps: List the partition table and table information for /dev/sdb.
Do not enter the interactive partitioning interface.
Hint: fdisk -l /dev/sdb

tasks.title: Create GPT Partition Table
steps: Start gdisk on /dev/sdb.
For commands use help by using ?
Use appropriate option to display the current partition table using gdisk.
Create a new GPT partition table on /dev/sdb. Follow the instructions given in task 4 and task 5
Warning: Creating a new partition table can destroy existing partition information. Make sure you are working on /dev/sdb.

tasks.title: Create Partitions
steps: Create the following partitions on /dev/sdb. For convenience GPT Partition Type is mentioned in Task 5 separately.
Create /dev/sdb1 with a size of 512 MB for swap.
Create /dev/sdb2 with a size of 512 MB Application data.
Create /dev/sdb3 with a size of 400 MB for Application logs.
Create /dev/sdb4 using the remaining available space for Backup.

tasks.title: Set Partition Type
steps: Set appropriate GPT partition type information for the partitions.
important_note: gdisk does not create a filesystem. The Hex Code changes the GPT partition type.
Set /dev/sdb1 as a Linux swap partition. Use GPT partition type 8200.
Set /dev/sdb2 as a Linux filesystem partition. Use GPT partition type 8300.
Set /dev/sdb3 as a Linux filesystem partition. Use GPT partition type 8300.
Set /dev/sdb4 as a Linux filesystem partition. Use GPT partition type 8300.

tasks.title: Verify and Save
steps: Display the partition table.
Verify that all four partitions have the correct sizes.
Verify that all four partitions have the correct GPT partition types.
Write the partition table to the disk.
Exit gdisk.
Execute 'partprobe' so the kernel detects the updated partition table without rebooting the system.

tasks.title: Verify From Linux
steps: Verify the newly created partitions using lsblk.
Inspect the partitions using blkid.
Use fdisk -l to display information about /dev/sdb.
Verify that /dev/sdb is using a GPT partition table.

tasks.title: Create Filesystems
steps: Create the appropriate filesystem or storage type on the partitions.
Initialize /dev/sdb1 as swap space
Create an XFS filesystem on /dev/sdb2
Create an ext4 filesystem on /dev/sdb3
Create an XFS filesystem on /dev/sdb4
Verify that the appropriate filesystem or storage type has been created on each partition.

tasks.title: Create Mount Points
steps: Create the /appdata directory for Application data.
Create the /applogs directory for Application logs.
Create the /backup directory for Application backup.
Verify that all the required mount-point directories exist.

tasks.title: Initialize swap space and Mount the Filesystems
steps: Mount the filesystems to their appropriate mount points.
Enable /dev/sdb1 as active swap space
Mount /dev/sdb2 on /appdata
Mount /dev/sdb3 on /applogs
Mount /dev/sdb4 on /backup
Verify that /dev/sdb1 is active as swap space.
Verify that /dev/sdb2 is mounted on /appdata.
Verify that /dev/sdb3 is mounted on /applogs.
Verify that /dev/sdb4 is mounted on /backup.

tasks.title: Configure Persistent Mounting
steps: Configure the filesystems and swap so that they are automatically available after a system reboot.
Configure /dev/sdb1 to be automatically enabled as swap at boot.
Configure /dev/sdb2 to be automatically mounted on /appdata at boot.
Configure /dev/sdb3 to be automatically mounted on /applogs at boot.
Configure /dev/sdb4 to be automatically mounted on /backup at boot.
Verify the persistent storage configuration without rebooting the system.
Reboot the system
After the reboot, verify that /dev/sdb1 is active as swap.
After the reboot, verify that /appdata is mounted automatically.
After the reboot, verify that /applogs is mounted automatically.
After the reboot, verify that /backup is mounted automatically.

completion_message: Great job! Lab 228 completed successfully. You practiced GPT disk partitioning, partition types, filesystems, mounting, and persistent storage configuration.
